userMessage.content: # ÓRBITA / Equipo para otros mundos Create a complete, highly art-directed Spanish-language ecommerce store for ÓRBITA, a fictional premium outdoor label inspired by retro space exploration and expeditions to Mars. This is wearable outdoor fashion and everyday equipment, not actual space-rated protective equipment. All product catalog data and supplied photographs are approved demo content. The website must be designed and implemented by pagosYa's AI generator. Make the composition memorable and specific to this brand. ## Creative direction Think of an expedition field manual transformed into a premium editorial store. Massive confident condensed grotesk typography, tiny monospaced equipment codes, thin technical rules, mission numbering, an orbital-circle insignia, warm bone #F0EEE6, ink #191B19 and saturated vermilion #EF451F. Real cinematic photography and generous whitespace. Square industrial controls with subtle clipped details. Use the campaign photograph at large scale, without covering the hiker. Hero headline: “EQUIPO PARA / OTROS MUNDOS.” Small kicker “ÓRBITA / EXPEDICIÓN 001”. CTA “Preparar mi expedición”. A quiet secondary link “Explorar la misión”. The first fold should feel like a magazine cover, with clear readable typography and visible equipment photography. A huge typographic ORBITA moment near the footer would reinforce the identity. Give the page a strong rhythm: compact technical navigation; cinematic campaign hero; narrow expedition information strip; beautifully photographed shop collection; striking vermilion editorial mission section with huge typography and an orbit/trajectory motif; practical buying FAQ; impressive typographic footer. Every section must feel like the same distinct brand. Avoid generic rounded cards, ubiquitous pill badges, purple gradients, emoji, fake reviews, fake certifications and meaningless metrics. Fictional mission labels are visual storytelling, not scientific claims. Include a subtle “Colección conceptual · Tienda de demostración” footer note. ## Real shopping experience Use the four EXISTING catalog products with all their saved variants, prices, inventory and extras. Do not recreate or duplicate them. Each product card opens its own product detail page. Add a visible cart count and usable cart/review route. Product detail layout: big product photo, small equipment code, product name, price that reacts to choices, short description, separate clearly labeled groups of options, optional additions with their prices, quantity, and a strong add-to-cart button. Group selectors by Color, Talla, Corte, Capacidad, Kit, Tapa, Misión, Presentación, Estuche as appropriate. Never flatten all combinations into one huge dropdown. Support available versus sold-out combinations, selected states, extras, mobile usability, keyboard focus and persistence of selected variant/extras in the cart. Prices in bolivianos, Bs. No purchase is to be automatically completed. The supplied photographs show the featured color; alternative colors are catalog options, not additional supplied photos. Preserve the product photograph without applying artificial color filters. Make this clear once in product details as “Fotografía del color de portada”. Parka = bone-white jacket photo; Mochila = vermilion backpack; Botella = graphite flask; Kit = pouch and patches flatlay. Never confuse the campaign photo with a product photo. Design the product and checkout pages with the same orbital identity, typography and industrial precision as the homepage. Reuse the supported pagosYa commerce runtime hooks for stock, variants, extras and checkout; ensure authored CSS also styles the commerce elements. Keep any native runtime controls functional. Use semantic HTML and responsive layouts at 390px and 1440px. No horizontal overflow, unreadable text over photos, hidden essential controls or dead navigation. Motion should be restrained: a slow orbital line or small entrance transitions, respecting reduced motion. ## Business content Brand statement: “Diseñamos equipo para quienes siempre miran un poco más allá.” Capsule collection: “Expedición 001 / Terreno desconocido”. Mission section: “LA CURIOSIDAD ES NUESTRO NORTE.” Supporting copy: “Una colección de prendas y objetos cotidianos inspirada en los paisajes de otro planeta. Para salir, explorar y volver con una historia.” The imaginary field-guide voice can use headings such as “Elige tu equipo”, “Configura tu misión”, “Lista de carga” for cart, and “Registro de expedición” for checkout, with familiar buying labels nearby for clarity. Do not invent shipping promises, discounts, contact details or warranty claims. FAQ can accurately explain choosing options, displayed prices, selecting extras, and that this is a concept demo. Please create the finished site now. You have complete creative authority within this brief and do not need additional preferences. ## Required implementation corrections from pagosYa validation The previous API attempt failed with: "product necesita data-cart-open en JSX visible." If generating Next/JSX, EVERY page module (home, product and checkout) must contain its own directly visible, literal `` in the JSX returned by that page, rather than relying only on an imported shared header. Preserve all other required commerce markers from the platform instructions. Reuse and complete the intended design, satisfying validation before saving. Catalog update: optional additions are now represented by a FOURTH variant group named Complementos, with four choices (Sin complementos, first add-on, second add-on, Kit completo). Their prices are already included in each saved variant amount. There are 312 total purchasable combinations across the four products. There are no separate extras arrays. Use the native grouped variant selectors for all four groups; do not send customers to the standard fallback product configurator. Do not change or duplicate the catalog. Preserve the actual price and stock for each combination. The three base option groups remain exactly as described above. steps.label: Comprobando el código y los recursos

answers.context: ÓRBITA es una tienda conceptual premium en español de ropa y equipo outdoor cotidiano inspirada en expediciones retrofuturistas a Marte; no presenta los productos como equipo espacial certificado. Público: personas de 20 a 40 años interesadas en diseño y aventura. Acción principal: explorar, configurar variantes reales y añadir al carrito. Identidad: manual editorial de expedición, hueso #F0EEE6, tinta #191B19 y bermellón #EF451F; grotesca condensada de gran escala, códigos monoespaciados, reglas técnicas, numeración de misión, motivos orbitales, controles industriales cuadrados y fotografía real. Frase principal: “EQUIPO PARA OTROS MUNDOS”. Colección: “Expedición 001 / Terreno desconocido”. Contenido confirmado: “Diseñamos equipo para quienes siempre miran un poco más allá.”, “LA CURIOSIDAD ES NUESTRO NORTE.” y “Una colección de prendas y objetos cotidianos inspirada en los paisajes de otro planeta. Para salir, explorar y volver con una historia.” Usar los cuatro productos existentes sin recrearlos ni duplicarlos: Parka Cráter 01 (120 variantes), Mochila Rover 02 (72), Botella Órbita 03 (72) y Kit de Misión 04 (48): 312 combinaciones reales en total, con cuatro grupos de variantes por producto y Complementos como cuarto grupo; conservar IDs, precios, stock y combinaciones. No hay extras separados. Fotografías aprobadas: campaña marciana como hero; parka hueso, mochila bermellón, botella grafito y kit con estuche/parches como fotos de producto. Las fotografías representan el color de portada, no deben recolorearse y debe indicarse una vez en cada detalle: “Fotografía del color de portada”. No inventar envíos, descuentos, reseñas, certificaciones, garantías, disponibilidad, direcciones ni datos de contacto. Incluir “Colección conceptual · Tienda de demostración” en el footer.
